newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria budget deficit up to 330 bln lvs April 30.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria budget deficit up to 330 bln lvs April 30.

text.p: Bulgaria's central government budget deficit rose by some 39 billion levs in the second half of April to 330.18 billion levs, a Finance Ministry official said on Friday, quoting preliminary figures.
"The deficit rose to 330.18 billion levs on April 30 mainly due to payments on government securities," the official, who
declined to be named told Reuters.
The Finance ministry made a total of 30.023 billion levs interest and discount payments on government securities in the second half of April, Finance ministry figures showed.

Deficit at end-April was around 1.59 percent of the nominal Gross Domestic Product (GDP) for 1997 assumed in a funding arrangement between the interim government and the International Monetary Fund (IMF) sealed in March.
Under the arrangement the budget deficit for this year was assumed at 3.8 percent of projected nominal GDP set at 20.743 trillion levs, down a real 4.8 percent from 1996.

Figures for spending, revenue and deficit as percentage of budget targets are not available because a viable 1997 budget has yet to be passed by the new parliament which assembled for the first time this week after April 19 election.

Bulgaria's macroeconomic performance has improved in the past month and the 1997 budget frame agreed between the IMF and the interim cabinet in March will need to be adjusted to the new indicators, government officials said.
Under a stop-gap budget bill approved on January 31 the deficit was limited to the volume of interest and discount payments on treasury paper. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 91188
